★彡 4.25 stars 彡★

“For all the readers who asked for an encore—this one’s for you.”


-ˋˏ✄┈┈┈┈ Question: Will physically shaking Axie Oh make another one of these books drop out of thin air?

Answer: If yes, then y’all better physically restrain ME from doing exactly that ᕕ( ᐛ )ᕗ

Granted that I’m lucky enough to have read the sweetest book with my sweetest bestie Maria! That’s how it’s DONE DONE DONE! ¬‿¬

ASAP is as deep as it is simple. Written deceptively like a sweet ‘n silly romcom, this book is filled to the brim with angst, ballads of self-discovery and self-love. It was a story made to be experienced and felt while still delivering all the sharp wit and goofiness you would expect of a YA romcom. Ain’t that the perfect package? >ᴗ<

⋮ ⌗ ┆ ᏖᏒᎧᎮᏋᏕ ᏗᏖ ᏇᎧᏒᏦ ⋮ ⌗ ┆

─•─ 𖦤 Friends To Lovers ♪♡

─•─ 𖦤 Second Chance Romance . ♬ ݁˖

─•─ 𖦤 Forbidden Romance ♪♡

─•─ 𖦤 Celebrity Couple . ♬ ݁˖


⋮ ⌗ ┆ ᎷᎩ ᏖᏂᎧᏬᎶᏂᏖᏕ ⋮ ⌗ ┆

: ̗̀➛ 🅣🅗🅔 🅢🅣🅞🅡🅨 & 🅣🅗🅔 🅕🅔🅔🅛🅢: Min Sori has had a dream for so long. To make people happy. To make the masses smile just because she exists. She used to think that being an idol was the key to unlocking this unspoken of a wish. She was so sure of it. But with every day, every realisation, she stills. She already has enough on her plate: from coming to terms with her rekindling feelings for a certain heartbreaker, fixing her mother’s company, to even fixing the gaps in her life. Funny how she does it all with a real smile ♡

I’ve said it once and I’ll say it again: second-chance and I don’t mesh well because most of the times, the reasonings behind the breakup are either too hard for me to forgive or too silly for me to take seriously. Few second-chances toe the perfect line of believably angsty and ASAP did it brilliantly with Sori and Nathaniel having a second round at it. To renewing their friendship and dealing with every reason that made them break up in the first place.

Shoutout to besties Aira, Astra and Salma: You guys, I’m a reformed woman… I think I’ve learnt to warm up to second-chances (ᴗ_ᴗ.) #ReadyToJoinTheClub

Besides the romance, the story is also strong in delivering Sori’s heartfelt journey through her lively lenses.

: ̗̀➛ 🅜🅘🅝 🅢🅞🅡🅘: Also known as the love of my pathetic little life. Hell, I thought I adored her in XOXO as a side character. I wasn’t prepared to fall on my knees for her. Damn this pathetic little heart ~

Sori’s a model, a glam queen. She sparkles on the outside for sure, but on the inside? Even more. What’s depressing funny is how people look at her and see an Ice Queen. She’s literally described as a cold beauty, someone who looks mean.

“I gained a reputation as someone stuck up, who thought she was better than everyone else.”


Wouldn’t you be surprised to know that she’s a squishmallow. This girlie here is easily the most adorable FMC that comes to mind. While she is crazily strategic and calculates the pros and cons of every potential move she could make, she also acknowledges that she’s a liar, a manipulator at times. She openly admits to herself that she is fake and uses people when desperate times call for it. That touch of darkness makes her all the more loveable because despite this, she’s truly willing to help and give to people she loves. She’s a lover and she loves wholly.

She is also an endearingly sensitive individual. She loves cutesy things and gosh the urge to crush her with a hug for HOW ADORABLE she is was off the charts! For example, she’s addicted to collecting stuffed animals and when stuffing one in her bag, she leaves it a little open, because-

“He can’t breathe if it’s zipped all the way.”


#RightsForStuffedOnes

“I want to need someone, just as much as I want to feel needed.”


Somehow it touched all the raw parts of me, because Sori is unabashedly craving love. More or less love-starved her entire life, she knows how much every relationship means. She loves those around her, and also loves herself to the fullest:

“Thanks, Sori-yah. You would have made a great idol, you know.”

“Maybe. But I think I’m a little too selfish. I want to make myself happy first, and I want to give myself only to a few people, not everyone.”


I’m not ashamed to admit that this girl has my heart. And I’m pathetically in love with her, did I mention? ಥ﹏ಥ

: ̗̀➛ 🅝🅐🅣🅗🅐🅝🅘🅔🅛 🅛🅔🅔: This guy not being real is almost as big of a crime as a white M&M! don’t ask me… yes, they’re a thing, AN ABOMINATION ⁽⁽(੭ꐦ •̀Д•́ )੭*⁾⁾

I’ll hear no judgment from anyone when I say I’m unabashedly into bad boys… of any and every kind. I. Said. No. Judgment. (≖_≖ )

Unbuttoned shirts, rolled up sleeves, stylishly mussed up hair… and a crooked crooked smile. I’m a basic bitch like that, so it ALWAYS works. Now take the blueprint of a classic bad boy and dial it up to the max. That’s Nathaniel Lee for ya, folks (づ ̄ ³ ̄)づ

“You should be wary about setting rules with me,” he says, his voice like silk. “You know I live to break them.”


*insert INTENSE sunburn emoji*

“I didn’t want to chase you,” he says, and I wince. Did he finally realize I’m not worth chasing? “I wanted to run with you.”


Real guys? For the sake of civility at least: TAKE. SOME. DAMN. NOTES.

Also, remember how I might have mentioned Sori’s obsession with her stuffed animals? Right after Nathaniel throws one of her Pikachu stuffed ones on the floor wanted to choke him to death for that, obsessed or no he says:

“I’ll apologize to each and every one of your stuffed animals if that’ll make you happy.”


Dude, marry me already, I’m down on my knees (ᴗ_ᴗ.)

When he’s not communicating in flirtsome language, you can find him being the poster child for PATIENCE. Quiet yearning? Nah, besties… make it iN yOuR fAcE kind of yearning. He gets rejected over and over and he’s still present in her life, as a friend. Just waiting for her signal that she wants more and he’ll give his ALL. They don’t make guys this perfect, anymore!

Finally, that mermaid scene (iykyk and boy do you wanna know ¬‿¬) was the single-most attractive thing I have read about. In my entire life. Like ever. Period. did I emphasise on it enough?

»»——★ fιnαℓ тнσυgнтѕ ★——««

➳ Maybe it’s just me being my usual brand of delusional, but I think we might be getting a third book on a certain boy-next-door and the maknae of our new girl group? Or maybe, it’s just me being… y’know… delusional >ᴗ<

then we kiss, and you know I won’t ever tell

I’m humbled. I thought I would have the same meh feeling about this as I did the author’s other books, and bought it solely for the cover. but boy, was I wrong. this was just about the cutest thing ever.

the reason that axie’s other books were a miss for me was because of the writing style, and unfortunately, that’s usually not something that varies from book to book; an author’s writing is what can make them well-loved or well-hated, because it has a distinct impression or voice. From my previous experiences with axie’s writing, I knew it to be cheesy and a bit stilted, and frankly incapable of writing chemistry or angst. imagine my surprise when the writing style in this book was not only fun, easy-to-read, and flowed remarkably well, but had a sizzling romance (not in regards to spice, obviously, as it’s YA, but in that the chemistry was immaculate).

sori and nathaniel are both, well, extremely hot characters and their moments actually had me silently squealing and cackling. I say this a lot, because I’m a hopeless romantic and almost anything remotely related to romance will make me pass out, but seriously; it was too good! I felt like I was watching a k-drama. the pool scene?? unwell. I loved how nathaniel didn’t force himself onto sori but waited patiently for her and respected her boundaries. They were such simps for each other and I was eating it up.

I also loved the kpop-based plot. The xoxo band members are all cute (youngmin & hyemi spinoff when??) and it was refreshing to have a protagonist who knew what she was doing and how to handle herself while being scrutinized by the media. speaking of awkward and oblivious characters… what do you know, I liked jenny a lot more when she wasn’t suffering from main character syndrome. She was actually really cute. The platonic & familial relationships in this book warmed my heart– sori had such cute relationships with jenny, hyemi, and her mom. we stan!!

–bottom line: this book really is just as cute as its cover <3

❝ I would walk the same path every lifetime, if I knew that at the end of it, you were waiting for me. ❞

this was a super cute palette cleanser 🥰💙!! i enjoyed reading about sori & nathaniel’s relationship from time to time; it was a nice YA romance 🎀. however, i did have some complaints. the first 60% of the book was pretty boring — nothing piqued my interest 🙃. i really, really, enjoyed the last 40% of the book though. a huge complaint that i had throughout the entire book was i didn’t care about the relationship 🫠. i was more interested in the debuting of ASAP and the familial problems. thankfully, the last chunk of the book really convinced me of their relationship, which was a relief. another big problem that i had with this book was, i really hoped that we would get to see the realities of the k-pop industry, however we got none of that. i understand this wasn’t a main point & that this IS YA, but a little recognition would’ve let the book dive deeper — again, i understand this is YA. overall, this was a light & fun time that i flew through.

･:*:･ﾟ⁀➷ 3.75/5 ★

Such a fun read!! 💜💜 I absolutely devoured this & i’ve discovered that i absolutely love kpop romances hehe 🤭💐

Tropes:
🎤 Kpop romance
🎤 Second chance
🎤 Set in Korea
🎤 Both of them are famous

I really enjoyed XOXO and sori & nathaniel were definitely my fav side characters in that book, so i was so excited that they were getting their own book! And this was the perfect follow up to XOXO, it was sm fun 🫶🫶

ೃ⁀➷ Writing & plot:

I really really like axie oh’s writing style!! This is only my second book by her but the way she writes works so well for these cutesy romances- it’s pretty simple, but still has enough descriptions that i feel like i’m in the story. This book was honestly so bingeable and i could not put it down once i started it. I definitely want to read more by this author and “The Girl Who Fell Beneath the Sea” is really intriguing to me.

I also really enjoyed the storyline of this book! 🥰🥰 Having the kpop industry as the backdrop of the book was so perfect bc i find it so fascinating and it also meant the book had a good plot outside of the romance. The romance was definitely the main focus, but there were still other things going on, which i enjoyed 🌷✨️

ೃ⁀➷ Characters:

I honestly really liked the characters in this book! So glad sori and nathaniel got their own book 🥹🫶

➵ Sori: she’s a really good fmc! I love how she appears so cold and severe, but has sm more to her and i really liked reading from her pov. Her character development in this book was done really well 🥰🥰

➵ Nathianel: AHH I LOVE HIM 🤭🤭 honestly, he has intrigued me since xoxo (i actually liked him more than jaewoo sorry!!) and he did not disappoint me in this book 👀😮‍💨 He was super attractive but also so sweet & caring, and he carried this book for me 🥹💗

ೃ⁀➷ Romance:

➵ Sori and Nathianel: their romance was sooo cute omg 🥹🥹 I thought the second chance romance trope was done really well and they had so many good scenes!! 🌷✨️ The chemistry was definitely there. However, the only thing i didn’t like about their relationship was that it felt like sori kept pushing nathaniel away when it was obvious they both wanted a relationship again. The last part of the book felt like a really prolonged third act conflict and it was really annoying 🙈🙈

➵ Jenny and Jaewoo: their appearances were so wholesome, i’m glad they’re happy together 🥹❤️‍🩹

ೃ⁀➷ In conclusion:

I had such a great time with this book 🥹🫶 I would definitely this series if you’re looking for:

➷ Kpop!!
➷ Such cute romance
➷ Great characters
➷ Interconnected standalones

Idk if there are plans for more books in this series but i would honestly love to see books for the remaining xoxo members 🌷✨️

I love me some cutie asian lit romance and this one hit the spot 🤭 this was seriously such an adorable book, so lighthearted and fun! One of my fav things about this author's book are the settings, they only fuel my dreams to travel to Asia haha. The romance was so cuuute, I think more tension would've made it better though! But I actually enjoyed the second chance trope more than I would’ve thought, it kind of gives the same vibes as fake dating, it just has to be done right yk! My main issue, however, was with the writing, I thought it was a bit simple and lacking in any original characteristics. I think it is just the author’s style though, and while it’s not my favorite it does fit the story well!

🪐₊˚ ⋅꒱ the characters:
Sori: Sori is just the coolest omg!! She literally can do anything. I liked how we got to see a more vulnerable side of her at times, and it was impactful to see how she always put her parents and their company first, even though they often neglected to put her first. But I’m happy that Sori and her mom bonded in the end 🫶🏼 also her stuffed animal obsession was TOO CUTE
Natheniel: When the love interest is 100% your type 🤭 I loved Natheniel so freaking much ugh. My heart kind of broke for him, but it’s also so adorable how he literally loved Sori the entire time after they first broke up and he just had to worship her from afar 🥺. Very loyal, (very demure, very mindful) and such a green flag if you ask me.

₊˚꒰🎧꒱‧ plot…
this book felt a tad bit deeper than axie’s other book (xoxo), which was still great on its own. after learning about sorinathaniel’s break up in xoxo, I wanted to cry because honestly? they sounded like a dream. in this book, axie writes about sori and nathaniel’s second chance romance. we also see multiple pages about sori dealing with training to debut almost her whole life but deciding that’s not what she really wants. on nathaniel’s part, he’s trying mostly to balance out his personal and idol life, which isn’t the main focus since this was a single pov book. the development in these two’s relationship was such a slow burn and extremely angsty, it was amazing (but may not be everyone’s cup of tea yk).

₊˚꒰🎵꒱‧ thoughts…
let’s start off strong with stuff I liked and appreciated— the angst; the slowburb; the way nathaniel was the ‘little things’ kind of guy; sori’s fearlessness and insecurities; the plot problems and solutions. on the other hand, it would’ve been a five star read if they get together much sooner? and also, if idol life was explored a bit more? overall tho, it was such a cute read and definitely needs to be on your tbr asap! (the way I ate this up in one day should tell you everything <3)

nathaniel waiting for sori at the convenience store every single day with her favourite juice has got to be my top favourite sorinathaniel moment <3 other than that, when she reads her webtoon while lying on nathaniel’s side? ugh. I want that kind of moment, oh my god. and also, the ‘chin up, songbird’ letter from him to her?! epitome of cute book boyfriend-ery <3

₊˚꒰⭐️꒱‧ ending…
sori finally chose what her career’s gonna be and that was such a powerful move on her part since she spent a major part of the book trying to figure out what she wanted to do with her life next. it was the best kind of closure I hoped for. and the epilogue where she wrote the letter to jenny? stop because sorinathaniel are going to paris and milan together and i’m reading romcoms in my bef all alone? this is so unfair ;-;


— ⌗ ”it’s you and me, remember? we got this.” ᝰ.ᐟ

hello? axie, who’s letting you write the deepest characters ever?! you hit it out of the ballpark with sori’s character. her flawless and gorgeous exterior portrayed as confident and secure in her choices and herself, but she also has the family trauma and anxiety and is actually insecure about what she chooses with respect to her job? this dynamic of differing personality traits was absolutely amazing to read. the need for sori to bottle up her feelings when it comes to certain things was so.. raw and understandable, yk?

I’m on BookTube now! =)

My heart races. “Sori, what are these rules for?”
“They’re just … rules …”
My eyes dart to his and my breath catches at the look in his eyes. “You should be wary about setting rules with me,” he says, his voice like silk. “You know I live to break them.”

I honestly don’t know how Sori managed to stay away from Nathaniel for two years because this boy is as perfect as they come. He’s not only an idol, but also a brother, best friend and the living embodiment of a bad boy with a heart of gold. So in other words perfect boyfriend material. I suppose their love for each other was never the problem, though. It was obvious they still had feelings for each other ever since I read “XOXO” and I’m so glad Axie Oh graced us with an “encore”! Truth be told, I actually enjoyed this even more than I enjoyed the first book, which is quite the surprise because I didn’t expect to be as invested as I was.

”Thanks, by the way. For picking up my call.” And for playing along for as long as he did. He didn’t have to – it was a risk for him.
“I’ll always pick up your calls.”

Maybe it was because Sori’s and Nathaniel’s love-story is very different than all the other k-pop romances I read so far. Usually you get an idol falling in love with a fan or a person who doesn’t even know who they are. This time however they were friends that turned into lovers and then due to external circumstances went back to being friends again. It was a choice they made for their careers and as much as Nathaniel hated it, he still accepted Sori’s choice and respected her wishes and boundaries. Which is amazing, go get yourself a man like him! Seriously! I never thought I’d love a second chance romance that much but here we are and this is legit the first second chance romance I gobbled up like nobody’s business. To be fair, all the other romances I read who had the trope actually had good reasons why the couples weren’t together anymore and that often stands in the way of my enjoyment. Like if one of the characters cheated on the other, or left them with a mess to deal with on their own, I just can’t see past that and have a hard time shipping them together. Thankfully, none of that happened in here and this made it so much easier to love those two oblivious k-pop idols in love. XD

"There's a short pause, and then he says, "You never stopped being my friend." My heart feels almost too big for my chest, and I realize how much I needed to hear him say those words.

Another thing that made this intriguing, was the fact that they were both idols and working in the industry. While Sori has been a trainee for a very long time and didn’t officially debut as a member of a k-pop group, she still stood in the spotlight and took part in variety TV shows, worked as a model, coached future k-pop idols and had guest roles in k-dramas or TV spots. It was interesting to see that part of the industry because it’s something that isn’t talked about a lot. I mean as a fan you know that they go through a tough training and are usually trainees for years until they debut with their group, but it was interesting to see how active some of those trainees already are. Not just behind the scenes but also doing those little PR-stunts while building up their career. I mean Sori’s schedule was packed and this even though she mostly worked behind the scenes. Nathaniel on the other hand already was an established idol and had his hands full with many appointments, but also with a scandal that included his family.

"He's always giving me so much, and I give nothing in return. I'm supposed to be the wealthy one, but he's the one who's generous."

Nathaniel’s family and their dynamic was another fun aspect of the story and I loved that he had four sisters whose names all started with an “N” too. *lol* We had Nadine, Noemi, Nicole and Natalie. I suppose his parents were lucky there are so many names that have “N” as a first letter. His personal life in America was a sharp contrast to his idol persona in Seoul and it was great to see the difference. It was also awesome to see more of the XOXO band members and to get cameos of Jenny as well! I swear one of my favourite moments of the book was when they all took part in one of those typical variety shows and just to read about their antics was already so much fun!

”Youngmin-ah, what are you doing?” Jaewoo is laughing so hard he slides off the sofa to the floor. The text beneath reads: Choi Youngmin finds hiding places that even the producers couldn’t find.

The way the members of XOXO and the other idols acted gave me serious RUN BTS vibes and I grinned like crazy. Also, I loved Sori’s friendship with Sun because he was one of the XOXO members we didn’t get a lot of in the first book. Turns out he’s actually very funny and I loved his easy banter with Sori! There’s something very sarcastic and suave about him and I couldn’t help but be intrigued by his character. Maybe we’ll get a third book with Sun as the main character? I’d totally be down for that! Calm and collected men that get all flustered and insecure when they meet the love of their live is one of those things I’ll never get tired of and I’d love to see Sun fall head over heels.

Sun lifts a single brow. “When you put it that way,” he says slowly, “I don’t think anyone could deny you. Even I’m blushing a little.”
“Really?” I frown. “You look pale.”
“I’m blushing inside.”

As for the love story between Sori and Nathaniel: It was bittersweet and extremely frustrating at the same time. *lol* No, seriously! I shipped them so hard and wanted them to be together, because their chemistry was amazing! They were so good for each other and the way they worked together had a familiarity you only get after spending almost your whole life together. To watch them deny themselves the one thing they truly wanted was heart breaking and killed me whenever they were on page together. Nathaniel’s longing was excruciatingly tangible and since we were in Sori’s head, we got to see how much his mere presence affected her as well. I understood the #MinLee shippers in the book, because a chemistry like theirs was bound to be noticed by others!

”Gripping the edge of the pool, I lift myself out of the water and press my lips to his. It’s brief. I don’t have enough upper body strength to hold myself above the water for longer than a peck. My lips part. He gasps softly. When I release him, his lips follow mine, as if seeking more, but I’m already falling back into the water.”

Unfortunately, there were plenty of external obstacles in their way and their fans most definitely were the least of their problems. Sori’s situation was complicated because her mom was legit the CEO of a k-pop idol company and her dad was a political figure. No matter what she did, she was always in the spotlight and since a relationship with Nathaniel could have ended his career, she decided to do the sensible thing and kept away from him instead. Of course, this hurt both of them, but I think in a way this was good, because they had some time to grow into their roles and to figure out what they truly wanted to do with their lives. For instance Sori might have trained to become an idol her entire life, but two years later, she knew that she didn’t want to stand in the spotlight and rather preferred a role behind the scenes.

"I can't let you make this decision on your own. How do you know if this is what you really want?"
"I know it's what I don't want."

I’ve to be honest here, when Sori told her mom at the beginning of the book, I was very sceptical about her reaction. I thought her mother would indulge her for a while, but ultimately would try to persuade her not to throw it all away. Without spoiling anything, I was kinda surprised to find out that her mom wasn’t the baddie I thought her to be and after reading the book I have such high respect for this woman and what she built. To see this perspective added even more depth to the story and I honestly can’t say a single bad thing about this story! *lol* It was great and the topics that were addressed were multifaceted and important. In my humble opinion “ASAP” was a lot stronger than “XOXO” when it came to all the serious topics and issues that were addressed. It felt like a more grown up version and it probably was because it plays two years after Sori’s and Nathaniel’s break up and about a year after XOXO. (At least I think it’s about a year after.) As I already said, Sori and Nathaniel both had time to grow and to figure out who they are and that definitely worked in favour of their story.

”Why did you pick me for your team?” I ask.
“I didn’t want to chase you,” he says, and I wince. Did he finally realize I’m not worth chasing? “I wanted to run with you.” I catch my breath.

Still, with Sori taking care of Hyemi, a new idol that’s supposed to join ASAP, and the troubles of her mother’s company there was a lot on the line and if your heart wants something different than your mind to find your own path isn’t easy. Nathaniel as well as Sori struggled to find their footing, but it was great to see them not only fight for their careers and dreams but also for their love and a future together. I think the ending was perfect for them and very fitting!

”I love him. I can admit that to myself now. I’ve always loved him. I love his voice and I love the way he looks at me. I love his laugh and I love the way he makes me laugh. I love the way I feel when I’m around him, like the days are warmer, the nights more beautiful. I love him so much that it makes me want to throw everything else away, if only to be with him, for one more day, for one more minute, for one more breath.”

Conclusion:

I already enjoyed “XOXO” when I read it 2022, but I absolutely loved “ASAP”! Maybe it was the more mature vibes or the fact that we got a good glimpse behind the scenes of the k-pop industry. Maybe it were Sori and Nathaniel as a couple and their strong longing and sweet familiarity. I honestly don’t know. All I know is that I was so here for it and enjoyed every second of this book! If you want to read a more mature k-pop romance, with a good mixture of fun and heartbreak, well, then this one is for you! Happy reading!

__________________________________

Oh wow, this book was such a rollercoaster!
Poor Nathaniel and Sori! Like wow, they certainly didn’t have it easy.
I had a lot of fun exploring Sori’s world, though, so that was pretty nice!

*4.5*

ES QUE DE VERDAD NO SABEN LO QUE ESTE LIBRO SIGNIFICA PARA MI.

Leí XOXO en, fácilmente, la mejor etapa de mi vida. Recuerdo vividamente como me sentía y la felicidad que llenaba mi cuerpo, por lo que es imposible el no asociar un recuerdo muy bonito a ese libro, cuando literal lo leí en mi peak. Entonces se imaginarán mi emoción cuando se anunció este libro.

ASAP es la historia de Nathaniel y Sori, dos personajes que conocimos en el libro anterior. Ellos, a diferencia de Jenny y Jaewoo, tienen una situación un poco más... complicada, pues son ex novios y la realidad es que los sentimientos pasados no han muerto del todo. Cuando un escándalo envuelve a Nathaniel, Sori tiene la oportunidad de apoyarlo, y se dará cuenta que su corazón aún le dice cosas que ella creía olvidadas. Aunque no todo es sencillo, pues Sori, que antes tenía todo perfectamente bien planeado respecto a su futuro como Idol, se da cuenta que quiere llevar su vida por otro lado. Razón por la cuál NO DEBERÍA ESTAR PENSANDO EN SU EX.

Esta libro es un clásico de Axie Oh: personajes entrañables, un romance swoon-worthy y con una cualidad adictiva que solo ella sabe escribir. Digo, ¿que más quieres de un second chance romance situado en Seúl? Es un historia linda, atrapante y que te va a dejar suspirando por más al leer la química innegable entre los protagonistas.

AMO la dinámica entre los dos protagonistas, y me atrevería a decir que casi como la de Jenny y Jaewoo. Mientras los primeros eran star-crossed lovers, este second chance romance me tenía mordiendome la uñas. Y yo solo digo, aún quedan dos integrantes más de XOXO y veo muy posible un friends-to-lovers con uno de ellos así que Axie Oh... *guiño guiño*

El único pero que tiene el libro es que, al igual que XOXO, se me hizo un final un poco apresurado. Me sorprende esto porque, juzgando otro libro de Axie "The Girl Who Fell Beneath The Sea" esto no fue un porblema, pero con estos dos libros si. Me hubiera gustado un poco más de desarrollo, pero no quedo en lo más mínimo insatisfecho.

De verdad de las mejores cosas que me pudieron haber pasado es haber tenido la oportunidad de leer este libro antes. Es una verdadera joya y un libro que espero todos lean porque lo tiene bien merecido.
——
ENG
*4.5*

YALL REALLY DON'T KNOW WHAT THIS BOOK MEANS TO ME.

I read XOXO in easily the prime of my life. I vividly remember how I felt and the happiness that filled my body, so it is impossible not to associate a very nice memory with that book, apart from the fact that I adored it dearly. So you can imagine my excitement when this book was announced.

ASAP is the story of Nathaniel and Sori, two characters we met in the previous book. They, unlike Jenny and Jaewoo, have a slightly more... complicated situation, since they are exes and the reality is that past feelings have not completely died out. When a scandal surrounds Nathaniel, Sori has the opportunity to support and shelter him, and she will realize that her heart still tells her things that she thought she had left in the past. Although not everything is easy, because Sori, who before had everything perfectly well planned regarding her future as an Idol, realizes that she wants to lead her life in a different direction, reason why she SHOULD NOT BE THINKING ABOUT HER EX.

This book is an Axie Oh classic: endearing characters, a swoon-worthy romance, and with addictive quality only she knows how to write. I mean, what more do you want from a second chance romance set in Seoul? It is a beautiful, captivating story that will leave you yearning for more when reading the undeniable chemistry between the protagonists.

I LOVE the dynamic between the two leads, and dare I say almost like as much as Jenny and Jaewoo. While the first one was a "star-crossed lovers"-esq type of story, this second chance romance had me biting my nails and wishing for more, always more. And I'm just saying, there are still two more members of XOXO and I see a very possible friends-to-lovers with one of them so Axie Oh... *wink wink*

The only drawback that the book has is that, like XOXO, the ending felt a little bit rushed. I'm surprised at this because, judging from another Axie book "The Girl Who Fell Beneath The Sea" this wasn't a problem. , but with these two books yes. I would have liked a little more development, but I am not in the least dissatisfied.

Truly one of the best things that could have happened to me is having had the opportunity to read this book as an arc. It is a true gem and a book that I hope everyone reads because it so, so worth it.

Thank you netgalley for providing me with and advance copy of the book for review!

——
